_README: Reusable Eleven-Music RECIPES (regenerate-on-demand, not baked mp3s). Shared doctrine gate with music_library/_specs. Selectable only when status=approved AND mood allowed for the beat.

recipes.title: 01_The_Crucifixion_Foretold
recipes.prompt: Instrumental only — no vocals, no lyrics, no choir, no drums or percussion, no beat. Open with a single sparse solo piano, one note at a time over deep silence, with one bare sustained low cello/string drone held beneath it — an ancient, prophetic stillness, like words being written down a thousand years too early, distant and patient, holding breath. As the dividing of the garments arrives, let a lone cello rise low and aching over the piano, a slow held line full of grief but never melodrama — soldiers casting lots while a life is poured out, restrained cathedral sorrow, never tipping into triumph. Around the midpoint, when prophecy meets the cross "that the scripture might be fulfilled," fold in a soft warm pad swelling almost imperceptibly, a reverent hush of recognition, never triumphant. In the final third, as the suffering man is named and "laying down his life to win you back" lands, let the piano resolve into a single tender, hopeful chord — grace breaking quietly through the grief — held with the cello fading into open air, holy and unhurried, breathing out rather than swelling to victory.

recipes.title: 02_The_Mockers_Words
recipes.lens: Minimalist-Ambient — sparse, intimate — solo piano, soft pads, single cello, lots of space and breath
recipes.prompt: A sparse, reverent solo instrumental for solo piano, single cello, and a low breath of warm pad — no vocals, no lyrics, no choir, no drums or percussion of any kind, roughly sixty seconds. Open cold and exposed: a single piano note struck and left to ring into silence, then a few hollow, hesitant intervals carrying the weight of the mockers' taunt — bare, unresolved, ached, never sweetened, like a man surrounded by jeering faces. Around the midpoint let one low cello note enter underneath, holding steady as the same ancient mockery is recounted across a thousand years — an unmoving presence that refuses to flinch or rise, tension held without resolving. In the final third, as the taunt turns to revealed love — "He stayed because staying was the only way to deliver you" — let the cello swell with quiet, tender gravity and a faint warm low organ pad bloom beneath it, the piano resolving from minor into a slow, settled, warm major chord held open and still rather than triumphant, ending on one soft sustained tone that hangs and slowly fades into breath. Strictly instrumental, reverent throughout, never bombastic, never victorious — the sound of love that chose to stay.

recipes.title: 03_The_Forsaken_Cry
recipes.lens: Cinematic-Redemptive (USER-OVERRODE panel 2026-06-18: wanted a driving, weighty score for the gravity)
recipes.prompt: A bare, reverent instrumental for solo piano, single cello, and a low breath of warm pad — no vocals, no choir, no lyrics, no drums or percussion of any kind. Open in near-silence: a single hesitant piano note repeated with long aching pauses, sparse and lonely, the sound of one voice alone in the dark. As the forsaken cry is named ("my God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me"), let a single low cello enter aching beneath it, held dissonant and unresolved through the darkest center at the ninth hour, so the grief is never rushed or sweetened. At the turn — "even forsaken, he still calls God, my God" — let a second, consonant cello line answer the first in gentle thirds, like a thread of faith inside the dark, steadying and grounding the piano on a held minor that refuses to collapse. In the final breaths ("he was forsaken so that you never will be… the way home is open, and he opened it from the dark"), let the harmony resolve slowly from minor toward a quiet open major, the piano warming and the pad rising softly like first light through a doorway — tender and hopeful, full of quiet awe, never triumphant and never tipping into celebration over grief. Fade back gently into stillness on a single warm sustained chord that simply rests, like a way home left open. Keep it slow, intimate, sacred, strictly instrumental throughout.
recipes.notes: user override of the panel's Minimalist-Ambient; driving cinematic, reverent not triumphalist; level brought to -8dB by ear (voice clearest)

recipes.title: 04_Declared_To_The_Brethren
recipes.prompt: A reverent solo instrumental score — strictly instrumental, no vocals, no lyrics, no choir, no drums or percussion of any kind. Open low and hollow on the far side of grief: a single bowed cello and a faint sustained pipe-organ pedal-tone breathing in a vast empty space, the lingering ache of "forsaken" still in the air — sparse, held, with deliberate silence and breath between phrases, never wallowing. Around the 25-second mark, as the psalm turns from anguish to praise, a lone piano enters with a quiet rising figure and a warm viola answers it like a voice deciding to sing again — grace beginning to break through. Through the final third let the strings gather gently and the organ open into a full, glowing, holy warmth — a soft major resolve that feels like a risen embrace and a name being declared, never bombastic, never triumphalist, never a fanfare. Keep space and breath throughout the full sixty seconds, intimate and tender to the end. Close on a single sustained, settled, open chord that simply says "family" — the sound of being called home.

recipes.title: 05_He_Hath_Done_This
recipes.prompt: A cinematic orchestral instrumental score — reverent and sacred, no vocals, no lyrics, no choir, no drums, no percussion of any kind. Open on a lone cello over a deep sustained string-section drone and a faint church-organ pedal note, vast and filmic — the hollow weight of a final breath drawn on a cross, set in a great echoing space. A solo piano enters with two slow falling notes; beneath it low strings and a soft sustained horn swell deepen and widen the room. Near the midpoint, a warm viola line crosses over the cello like an answer arriving from far off — two voices a thousand years apart sounding the same note — and the full string section begins to gather underneath. From there build a slow, sweeping cinematic crescendo: layered warm strings rising in long bowed phrases, a glowing sustained horn line, and the pipe-organ opening beneath into a broad, holy, golden swell — epic and deeply moving, an overwhelming tide of relief and completion, yet never a triumphalist fanfare and never bombastic. Let it crest on a full, sustained, radiant major chord that feels like the whole sky opening over the finished work, then ease gently back to a solo piano and one last glowing sustained string chord that simply rests — finished, at peace, a cinematic 'come home.' Rich orchestral depth, wide stereo image, warm cinematic reverb and air throughout.
recipes.notes: USER-APPROVED 2026-06-19 — full orchestral cinematic treatment (string section + horns + organ, sweeping crescendo, wide reverb); the NEW STANDARD for shorts, supersedes the sparse solo version.

recipes.title: 06_The_Ends_Of_The_Earth
recipes.prompt: Reverent instrumental film score, strictly instrumental — no vocals, no lyrics, no choir, no drums or percussion beat — about sixty seconds, holy and unhurried. Open bare and aching: a single unaccompanied cello holding a low, lonely minor line under sustained string-pad shadows and a distant solo piano, spacing the notes wide over near-silence — the sound of one man dying utterly alone in a corner of an empire. Around the halfway hinge, exactly where the song throws its arms open to the nations, let warm violins and a soft horn enter and gently lift the harmony from minor toward open, hopeful major, as if arms slowly opening outward — grief turning to promise, never abrupt. Then swell wide and full: layered strings, tender low brass, glowing piano arpeggios spreading like the gospel reaching nation after nation — a reverent, awestruck, expansive crescendo that conveys vast reach, never brash or triumphalist, no fanfare. In the final moments resolve back to tender intimacy: a single piano and one held string note, soft and inviting, leaving real room and breath — an unhurried, personal call to turn home that reaches "wherever you are" without ever crowding it.

recipes.title: 07_The_Body_Foretold
recipes.prompt: A reverent instrumental score, strictly instrumental — no vocals, no lyrics, no choir, and no drum or percussion beat or pulse of any kind. Open cold and exposed: a single hollow sustained cello drone with a thin tremolo high-string shimmer above it, sparse and unresolved — almost forensic in its quiet — conveying a body poured out like water and bones pulled loose. As an ancient king's eyewitness wonder unfolds, let a low piano lay slow, widely-spaced single notes over the strings, thinning to bare suspended intervals so the music feels stretched and exposed — the dread of a dying man being counted bone by bone and stared upon — the harmony tightening into aching dissonant suspensions that refuse to land, the grief held and never resolved. Then, precisely on "this is what Jesus bore to bring you home... crushed in your place," let warm legato strings and a soft horn swell rise up beneath the cello, the suspensions finally resolving into a tender, holy major as a delicate felt-piano or harp figure rises like dawn — never triumphalist, never loud, just grief turning to grace, the suffering revealed as deliberate substitution. Close on a single sustained string chord held in awe, soft and unhurried, breathing out and settling into stillness.

recipes.title: 08_I_Thirst
recipes.prompt: A sparse, reverent instrumental score for solo piano, a single low cello, and the faintest warm pad — strictly no vocals, no choir, no drums or percussion beat — built almost entirely of silence and breath. Open with two slow, bare piano notes set far apart, like a parched mouth shaping the words "I thirst," each note left to decay fully into emptiness. As the body fails ("my strength is dried up like a potsherd... brought me into the dust of death"), the cello enters very low and dry, a long aching unresolved tone, the piano thinning to single cracked notes with wide gaps between them — dust, dried clay, a man sinking. At the gospel turn — the One who made every river hanging dry, "in your place," offering living water — let a few glassy single droplets of a hammered dulcimer or harp fall sparse and bright, like the first trickle of water, while one warm sustained pad blooms underneath and the cello rises a gentle fourth into a tender, hymn-like resolve — grief lifting into mercy, reverent and never triumphant. Close on a single held piano chord over the soft pad, the dulcimer notes ringing away, fading slowly to silence — the holy hush of a gift given, water that never fails.

recipes.title: isaiah_53_5_with_his_stripes
recipes.prompt: A reverent instrumental film-trailer underscore for a 60-second meditation on Isaiah 53:5 — strictly instrumental, no vocals, no choir, no lyrics, and no drum or percussion beat of any kind. Open in bare stillness on a single aching solo cello over sparse, suspended felt-piano, an unresolved minor suspension left hanging — the sound of a wound that keeps reopening — then let a low sustained string drone carry the ancient weight of "seven hundred years before the cross," dignified sorrow only, never melodramatic. As the flogging and the stripes are named, hold the grief reverent and unhurried, the cello bowed low and heavy, restrained, never swelling into drama. At the turn — when Peter lays Isaiah's words on Christ and points "ye were healed" straight at the listener, at you — let warm strings bloom underneath and the harmony lean slowly from minor toward an unhurried major, grace breaking in like dawn through stone, not a fanfare. Through the final lines — "He has already closed... come to Him, and receive it" — swell gently to a holy resolve of warm strings and soft horn warmth, the grief honored before the grace breaks in, never triumphalist. Close on a single glowing sustained, resolving warm chord that settles and releases, tender and finished, holy and at rest.

recipes.title: mockers_words_ps22
recipes.prompt: A reverent instrumental film-trailer underscore in a minor key, strictly no vocals, no lyrics, no choir, no drums or percussion, no beat — only strings, low piano, and a single soft distant horn, over about sixty seconds. Open in cold ache: a single muted cello and a lone sustained violin over hushed, thin low strings — sparse and bare, carrying the sting of the mockers' jeering, head-shaking taunts ("let him deliver him... if you really are the Son of God") and the loneliness of the cross; restrained and hollow, never bombastic where grief is due, letting the scorn pile on into a held, aching dissonance that does not resolve. Around the turn — "He proved He was the Son not by escaping but by staying on it" — let a low piano enter with slow, falling single notes, like words landing one at a time, and a warm cello line begin to rise underneath, holding tension as the strings deepen: the weight of chosen suffering, pressing down rather than crashing. In the final third, as grace breaks in — "He stayed under their scorn, and yours, to win you... Come to the One who would not come down" — let the strings and a soft, distant low-brass horn swell into an aching but resolving major warmth, holy and tender rather than triumphalist, grace breaking in quietly. End on one sustained, settled major string chord that hangs open and unresolved on the invitation — soft and open like a held breath or an outstretched hand, never a victory fanfare.

recipes.title: zechariah_12_10_pierced
recipes.prompt: A strictly instrumental sacred ambient score for a 60-second gospel short — absolutely no vocals, no choir, no lyrics, and no drums or percussion of any kind, reverent and intimate throughout. Open cold and isolated: a single bare solo piano note left hanging in silence, like the point of the spear going into a dead man's side, joined by a low breathing pad as the dread of a five-centuries-old sentence settles. As the verse turns ("they shall look upon me whom they have pierced"), let a lone unaccompanied cello rise in a slow grieving line over the piano — aching and unresolved — and beneath it allow a low sustained cello/viola drone to breathe (the ancient weight of the prophecy), leaving long gaps of empty air between phrases so the weight of "God says they pierced Me — then, mourn for Him" can land like one mourning for an only son. Keep the harmony hollow and unresolved here so nothing triumphal intrudes on the mourning. At the exact moment grace breaks in ("not with wrath, but with grace poured out"), let warm sustained strings and a soft pad bloom gently upward from minor into a tender, holy major resolution — luminous and forgiven, never victorious or loud, opening like dawn rather than a fanfare. Then settle back to intimacy and close under "Look at Him — and live" on a single soft piano chord ringing out into stillness — an open invitation, not a swell, fading to one held note and silence.
